The duel proves that Blood Knight power can withstand a shaman’s full assault, strike with overwhelming force, and remain governed by skill, command, and martial honor, while leaving M’uru’s captivity unresolved.

nodes.label: The high priestess at the inner gate

properties.summary: During a retreat through an inner-gate evacuation point, Falanaras briefly sees High Priestess Liadrin working among the wounded. She steadies frightened survivors, calls on the Light with practiced faith, and spends its golden radiance on healing even as the defenses fail around her. He knows her chiefly by office and reputation, but the image remains with him: a priestess still trusting grace amid the kingdom’s ruin before she continues toward the final defense of the Sunwell.

Because contact had seemed steady only days before, the sudden silence feels less like distance than rupture; Falanaras watches confidence in Kael'thas begin to curdle as citizens argue whether the prince is endangered, betrayed, or withholding the truth.

As Liadrin's guard, Falanaras is present for crackdowns meant to prevent panic and factional collapse, and he struggles with the sight of Silvermoon defending itself not only with Blood Knights and magisters but with fear, arrests, and magically compelled obedience.

nodes.label: Preparation for Tempest Keep reveals three philosophies

properties.summary: As the retinue reaches Netherstorm and settles into the siege camps outside Tempest Keep, Rommath, Astalor, and Liadrin each reveal a different answer to blood elf survival: arithmetic of state, mastery of power, and hard resolve in carrying through what necessity demands.
Silvermoon formally resolves that Kael'thas can no longer be relied upon, and its forces are instructed to treat his faction in Outland as unfriendly.

Before the founding, Falanaras, Theron, and Lethira speak privately about the new order. Falanaras and Theron state that they intend to become Blood Knights. Lethira answers with dry finality, ‘No thanks. I’ll stick to my bow.’ She has no interest in changing callings and treats the choice with the certainty of a ranger content with her own weapon.

News of the severance spreads through Silvermoon in controlled proclamations and private shocks, but many citizens refuse the official account, insisting Kael'thas is being slandered or that Outland remains the promised road of their people. Banners bearing the prince's phoenix come down from official halls while arguments flare in taverns, temples, and mana queues.

properties.description: Lor’themar, Liadrin, Lethira, Falanaras, and their attendants travel under Forsaken escort through the Ghostlands to ruined Windrunner Spire. Sylvanas offers to advocate for Silvermoon before the Horde and demands that Tranquillien be cleared and rebuilt as a joint base of operations. Lor’themar and Lethira accept joint use while preserving Quel’Thalas’s sovereignty through paired blood elf–Forsaken command, agreed garrison limits, jointly counted stores, advance warning before movement toward Eversong, and defined anti-Scourge objectives. Sylvanas also weighs the Blood Knights as proof that the blood elves may be useful allies.
properties.summary: Lor’themar, Liadrin, Lethira, Falanaras, and their attendants travel under Forsaken escort through the Ghostlands to ruined Windrunner Spire. Sylvanas receives them in the remains of her ancestral home, where her presence forces the delegation to confront both the Banshee Queen and the former Ranger-General who still claims an interest in Quel’Thalas. She offers to advocate for Silvermoon before the Horde, demands that Tranquillien be cleared and rebuilt as a joint base of operations, and treats the Blood Knights and the defense of the Ghostlands as proof that the blood elves may be useful allies. The negotiated terms preserve blood elf sovereignty while establishing paired command, agreed garrison limits, shared stores, and coordinated action against the Scourge.

nodes.label: Orders and march toward the runestone boundary

properties.description: Reports of Amani movement and disturbed Scourge forces send Liadrin’s first Blood Knights south with Lethira’s rangers. They ride hawkstriders through restored Eversong before meeting Serenya, knowing the runestone boundary marks the edge of maintained territory and that the Ghostlands beyond remain wholly hostile.

nodes.label: Liadrin's creed persuades Falanaras and reaches Theron differently

properties.summary: Through private conversation and example, Liadrin teaches Falanaras to carry the burden without pretending purity, while Theron responds more simply to the order's promise of disciplined strength in service to Quel'Thalas.

The returning high elves react sharply to the blood elves' new name, altered path, and visible dependence on fel energies, and Falanaras feels pride, defensiveness, and shame collide as grief over the dead becomes inseparable from political, cultural, and magical severance.

properties.description: Immediately after the ruined-way-station battle, the exhausted unit reaches Halduron Brightwing’s forward command post at the Eversong–Ghostlands border and reports the Argent Dawn incursion, Serenya Duskrunner’s Dark Rangers, the standoff, and the recovered command focus. A courier interrupts with Kael’thas’s summons. Halduron orders one full day of in-camp rest before analysis of the focus produces a final covert assignment into Deatholme, making clear that existing duty in the Ghostlands will not be abandoned for the prince’s call.
properties.summary: Before any departure to Outland, Falanaras's team is assigned a final covert operation into Deatholme, making clear that existing duty in the Ghostlands war will not simply be abandoned for the prince's summons.

properties.description: Partway through the operation, Captain Rynel’s long-concealed loss of control erupts inside Deatholme’s lower vaults. He feeds compulsively from Scourge acolytes, continues drawing after their active spells are gone, breaks the team’s stealth, and turns on Falanaras when interrupted. With his disciplined bearing stripped away, his gaunt face, overbright eyes, hunched posture, and hooked hands resemble the early Wretched. His comrades still recognize the man within that decline, but can no longer mistake where his hunger is taking him.
properties.summary: Inside Deatholme’s lower vaults, Captain Rynel loses control of his magical hunger and feeds compulsively from Scourge acolytes, continuing after their active spells are exhausted. He breaks the team’s stealth, turns on Falanaras when interrupted, and emerges gaunt, hunched, overbright-eyed, and visibly close to the Wretched decline he once taught his soldiers to fear.

properties.description: Captain Rynel Starweaver personally selects Falanaras for command-magic disruption, Theron for holding a broken line, and Lethira for tracking, then brings them to a war-table briefing with Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing. Halduron briefs them only on the mobile Scourge remnant and the uncertain southern border; the Argent Dawn and Forsaken patrols remain unknown until encountered in the field.
properties.summary: Rynel selects Falanaras, Theron, and Lethira for complementary field skills and brings them before Halduron for a briefing on a mobile Scourge threat. They enter the Ghostlands with no warning that Argent paladins or Forsaken Dark Rangers are operating nearby.

nodes.label: Lethira between the spire and the throne

properties.summary: After the Undercity audience, Lethira and Falanaras compare the Sylvanas who stood amid the ruins of Windrunner Spire with the Banshee Queen enthroned beneath Lordaeron. The ancestral setting exposed terrible fragments of the ranger-general who once defended Quel’Thalas; the undead capital reveals the ruler she has made from what Arthas left. Lethira is shaken because neither image cancels the other: Sylvanas is a desecration of the woman they remember and, in cold and commanding fragments, still recognizably herself.

Travelers and couriers preparing to pass through the Dark Portal report that it snapped shut without warning in front of them, severing routes to Outland in an instant and leaving families, commanders, and magisters scrambling for explanations.

nodes.label: Sylvanas receives them in her seat of power

properties.summary: The party enters the Forsaken throne room for a formal continuation of the parley begun at Windrunner Spire. Here Sylvanas receives the blood elves as the ruler who must sponsor their case before the Horde, with Varimathras looming behind her as a courtly demonic presence and a visible reminder of the compromises already tolerated inside Horde-aligned power. When Rommath, or another sharp-tongued elf, refers to him as Sylvanas’s pet, Varimathras reacts with anger and is immediately cut down by a cold rebuke from the Banshee Queen, clarifying both his danger and the fact that he survives here only under her command.

properties.description: After M’uru willingly enters the cage, Falanaras names the actual wrong: they intend to imprison a living being and take its Light into themselves. Liadrin does not question whether they will proceed. Drawing on her former devotion, she acknowledges the profanation without hesitation and insists that they say it plainly while remembering the soldiers, children, and starving people for whom they commit it. Her creed joins responsibility to action without seeking absolution.
properties.summary: Falanaras leaves Tempest Keep morally shaken by the rebuke at the shrine, but unable to reject Liadrin's logic: if even salvation comes stained, then someone must still choose to bear that stain for Quel'Thalas rather than pretend cleaner options remain.

As disbelief turns into unrest, Silvermoon imposes harsher order: patrols break up pro-Kael'thas gatherings, magisters arrest citizens who openly speak of leaving for Outland, and anti-Horde agitators are treated as threats to the kingdom's survival rather than mere dissenters.

Edric's golden Light follows the cadence Falanaras remembers from their fight in the Ghostlands: grounded stance, measured breath, brief invocation, a ward raised before the answering strike, and radiance gathered with restraint before release. Falanaras now meets that familiar discipline with the harsher red-gold power he draws through the Blood Knights' subjugation of M'uru. Their duel becomes a blinding collision no one else wants to enter, and the precise details Falanaras once observed without judgment finally reveal the fracture between Edric's paladin faith and his own chosen necessity.
A group of high elves from the diaspora arrives in Quel'Thalas with Vereesa Windrunner among them, returning at last to see what remains of their homeland and kin after the fall.

Within Silvermoon, M'uru is received as a possible answer to the whole population's magical hunger rather than a resource intended only for soldiers. Its ambient presence eases symptoms near the vault, and magisters test wardstones, healing foci, storage vessels, and distribution conduits toward clinics, ration halls, public wards, and common districts. The early systems remain unstable or inefficient, while the captive's suffering stays hidden below ground and rumors turn promised relief into public expectation.

Despite all the kingdom's compromises, Kael'thas remains a distant symbol of hope, and many cling to the belief that his return from Outland will justify what has been endured and solve what Silvermoon cannot.

nodes.label: Kael'thas seen in his altered element

properties.summary: By the time Falanaras finally reaches Netherstorm and enters the prince's war rooms, Kael'thas appears not as an awaiting savior at journey's end but as a commander already deep inside a larger campaign, reshaped by Outland, command, and proximity to powers Silvermoon would once have found unthinkable.

properties.description: Rynel breaks the ward-anchor after the others cross, collapsing the passage between the survivors and the pursuing Scourge. Falanaras, Theron, and Lethira escape Deatholme carrying the recovered intelligence, Rynel’s final command, and the knowledge that even near Wretched collapse he recovered enough discipline to take only what the defense required, stop while more remained, and spend the captured power on their survival.
properties.summary: Rynel breaks the ward-anchor after the others cross and collapses the passage. The survivors escape knowing that, even near Wretched collapse, he refused one final feed and chose disciplined sacrifice instead.

nodes.label: Demons make the Portal everyone’s war

properties.summary: The Burning Legion’s renewed control of the Dark Portal has become impossible for either Horde or Alliance to ignore. Demons pouring through the gateway are no longer contained at the threshold; raids and probing attacks have begun reaching settlements, supply routes, and military roads beyond the Blasted Lands, forcing both factions toward a wider response even as they remain enemies.
Falanaras, Captain Rynel, Theron, and Lethira begin the covert mission into Deatholme with the summons hanging over every choice.

nodes.label: The search for other allies begins in earnest

properties.summary: Once the prince is set aside, the necessity of finding outside allies becomes immediate and unavoidable.

nodes.label: Victory narrows toward the hidden shrine

properties.summary: After the larger clash turns in Kael'thas's favor, Falanaras and the retinue press inward through the fortress toward M'uru's inner chamber with victory and deliverance seeming at last to converge, until battlefield triumph gives way to a quieter and more terrible objective at the heart of Tempest Keep.

The letter explains that Voren'thal and the Scryers tried to persuade Kael'thas to heed the vision and turn away from ruin. As they defected from his command and Illidan's forces, Kael'thas answered the collapse around him by betraying Illidan in turn, seizing Tempest Keep and Netherstorm for himself and turning toward demonic power as a desperate alternative to the redemption Voren'thal had foreseen.

nodes.label: Training in a city of hunger

properties.continuityBoundary: This beat owns the essential bridge exposition displaced from Chapter 1: the Sunwell’s destruction, the sin’dorei naming, Kael’thas’s departure, and Lor’themar’s regency.
properties.description: Following the time skip, Falanaras trains as a spellbreaker in rebuilding Silvermoon. Early exposition delivered through his changed daily life establishes that Kael’thas returned after the invasion, destroyed the corrupted Sunwell with Rommath and Astalor, named the survivors sin’dorei, departed in search of aid, and left Lor’themar to govern in his absence.
properties.summary: Years later, Falanaras trains as a spellbreaker in a kingdom reshaped by Rommath's policies, where visible fel crystals and the normalization of siphoning have become part of daily life even as many still treat them as an ugly necessity rather than a triumph.

A Scryer messenger carries Voren'thal the Seer's letter directly to Lor'themar, bypassing ordinary channels and forcing the revelation into the center of state power. The letter describes Voren'thal's vision of a future in which his people rise free from addiction and despair, restored by the touch of a naaru's Holy Light over Quel'Thalas, and his conviction that Kael'thas's path through Illidan, conquest, and desperation cannot lead them there.

properties.chapterDetails: Chapter 1 presents the city's destruction through retreating witness; Chapter 2 shows reconstruction-era daily life under normalized fel use and hunger management; Chapter 3 turns the city into an object seen through high-elf eyes, intensifying its estranged self-consciousness.
properties.description: The shattered but rebuilding capital of Quel'Thalas, marked after the fall by visible fel crystals, social strain, and the constant pressure of magical hunger. Its beauty survives in repaired bridges, white stone, banners, and evening light, but daily life is defined by inspections, rationed feeding, watchful discipline, and the ever-present fear of wretched decline. Silvermoon is at once triumph, accusation, and habitat for compromise.
properties.invasionGeography: During the Scourge invasion, the dead attacked Silvermoon from the south along the Dead Scar. Southern flight was blocked; the western city and approaches were destroyed and overrun. Civilians and retreating defenders used side gates, with the eastern route becoming the successful escape corridor.

properties.description: An alien marshland crossed by the summoned blood elf retinue during its journey across Outland toward Netherstorm.

properties.chapter12Continuity: During Chapter 12, the Ghostlands remain wholly hostile. An Amani-driven Scourge host races north along the Dead Scar and crosses the restored runestone boundary into southern Eversong before the Blood Knights can intercept it. The battle and victory occur inside Eversong, not at Tranquillien.
properties.chapter13Continuity: Several months after the first Blood Knight deployment, the Ghostlands remain hostile and unheld. Blood Knights and Farstriders conduct dangerous missions south of the runestone boundary, withdraw after completing limited objectives, and coordinate only at a distance with Serenya’s Forsaken scouts through signals and fields of fire.
properties.chapter16Continuity: The Ghostlands remain hostile and broadly unheld during the Windrunner Spire negotiations. Forsaken scouts operate on its roads and share warnings with assigned blood elf units. The provisional terms commit both forces to clear and rebuild Tranquillien as a joint base under paired command, agreed force limits, shared accounting, and no separate Forsaken territorial claim. The delegation passes west of the still-empty town before this agreement is reached; the base is planned, not yet operational, by the end of Chapter 16.
properties.description: The blighted southern reaches of Quel’Thalas where blood elves fight the Scourge, first cooperate uneasily with the Forsaken, and undertake the Deatholme mission. At the time of the first Blood Knight deployment, the Ghostlands remain wholly hostile and no blood elf or joint force holds Tranquillien; patrols enter at great risk from the restored runestone boundary in southern Eversong.

The Amani troll stronghold in the Ghostlands. During the first Blood Knight deployment, raiders operating from its sphere of influence break Scourge control fetishes and drive a host north along the Dead Scar. The undead cross the restored runestone boundary before interception and are destroyed inside southern Eversong by Blood Knights, Farstriders, and Forsaken scouts; Tranquillien remains a hostile ruin.

properties.chapter12Details: An Amani-driven Scourge host crosses the restored southern runestone boundary before interception and enters Eversong along the Dead Scar. The first Blood Knights, Farstriders, and Serenya’s Forsaken scouts destroy the incursion within Eversong; the boundary still separates restored northern territory from wholly hostile Ghostlands.
properties.description: The enchanted northern forest surrounding Silvermoon. Its ancient runestone network ordinarily holds the woods in perpetual spring. In this project’s adapted continuity, Arthas’s invasion damaged that network badly enough for the natural seasons to return; survivors briefly endured winter before the restored runestones renewed the spring enchantment.
properties.seasonalContinuity: Project adaptation: After Arthas and the Scourge broke the runestone network, Eversong Woods lost its perpetual-spring enchantment and experienced a brief return of the natural seasons, including winter. During reconstruction, the blood elves restored enough runestones to reestablish the enchanted spring.

properties.description: The ruined human kingdom surrounding Undercity, devastated by the Scourge and claimed in part by the Forsaken. The Silvermoon delegation crosses its dead capital on the way to Horde judgment, and Falanaras’s duel with Gorath takes place in the shattered royal courtyard above the Forsaken city.

An Alliance-held town in Hillsbrad whose forces maintain constant pressure on Horde-held Tarren Mill. That conflict draws Falanaras’s sin’dorei detachment into its first campaign under Horde command and places Edric and Caelir among the opposing Alliance forces.

properties.chapter16Continuity: Windrunner Spire serves as the first formal parley ground between Silvermoon and Sylvanas. The ruined ancestral seat remains in the hostile Ghostlands, guarded temporarily by Forsaken archers but established as neither a permanent Forsaken garrison nor a territorial transfer. Sylvanas uses the site to confront the blood elves with her old claim as Ranger-General, her present power as Banshee Queen, and the transactional cost of Horde sponsorship.
properties.description: The ruined ancestral seat of the Windrunner family in the Ghostlands. Its position within wounded Quel'Thalas and its intimate connection to Sylvanas make it a symbolically charged meeting place for the first formal negotiations between Silvermoon and the Forsaken.

The human-led magical city where high elf exiles and other survivors gather after Quel’Thalas’s fall. It anchors Caelir and Vereesa’s distance from Silvermoon and forms part of Kael’thas’s history before his followers escape toward Outland.

properties.chapterDetails: Chapter 2 expands it from a troubled district into a sensory center of the city's magical desperation, sanctioned crystal houses, illicit practices, and intimate fear of losing control.
properties.description: A troubled district of Silvermoon where deprivation, illicit magical feeding, petty corruption, and the threat of wretched decline are especially visible. It survives by adapting quickly to bad necessities and serves as one of the clearest street-level embodiments of what post-Sunwell life has done to the sin'dorei.

The fractured Outland region surrounding Tempest Keep, where Kael’thas organizes the campaign to capture M’uru. It later becomes part of the territory he seizes after rejecting the Scryers’ warning and turning against Illidan’s forces.

properties.chapter14Details: After Kazzak reopens the Dark Portal for the Burning Legion, Hellfire Peninsula’s eastern threshold and ridges are occupied by demons. Concealed Farstriders find Legion emplacements, felhounds, altered or destroyed stabilizing engines, an abandoned Sunfury station, smoke over the northern works, and no blood elf formation holding the former road toward Kael’thas. Hellfire is open to passage under extreme risk but no longer functions as Silvermoon’s controlled entry into Outland.
properties.description: The blood elf retinue's point of arrival in Outland and Falanaras's first direct experience of Kael'thas's altered world.

A major bastion of the Light in the Plaguelands, associated here with the paladins who cross into the Ghostlands and reunite Falanaras with Edric Hale. Its paladins embody a disciplined devotional practice expressed through measured invocation, communal duty, protection, healing, and deliberate violence against the undead. Falanaras's close observation of their methods seeds details whose full significance emerges only after he becomes a Blood Knight.
The scarred region surrounding the Dark Portal on Azeroth, crossed by Falanaras and later threatened by demons pouring through the reopened gateway.

properties.chapter14Details: Shattrath becomes Silvermoon’s first meaningful source of Outland intelligence after the Portal reopens under Legion control. A Scryer messenger from the city reaches concealed Farstriders with Voren’thal’s authenticated letter and evidence, presenting Shattrath as both refuge for blood elf defectors and an alternate source of truth outside Kael’thas’s command.
properties.description: The city from which A'dal and allied blood elves such as the Scryers help relay intelligence about Kael'thas's turn in Outland. Though mostly offstage, it represents an alternate blood elf future and a source of truth beyond Silvermoon's isolation.

A major Scourge stronghold in the Ghostlands where Falanaras, Rynel, Theron, and Lethira infiltrate a necromantic records vault. Its linked ward-anchors provide the team’s intelligence objective and escape route; during the withdrawal, Rynel suppresses and severs one anchor to save his companions at the cost of his life.
The reconstruction-era training yard and barracks where Falanaras, Theron, and other recruits drill under Captain Rynel amid visible fel-crystal infrastructure and normalized hunger discipline.
The blighted path carved through Quel'Thalas by the Scourge, still channeling undead threats toward Silvermoon.
properties.directionalGeography: The Scourge advanced north along this route from the Ghostlands and Eastern Plaguelands into Silvermoon, then continued north toward Quel’Danas. The south therefore remained the invasion approach rather than a civilian escape route.

properties.chapter12Continuity: Tranquillien is not visited, defended, held, or reclaimed in Chapter 12.
properties.chapter13Continuity: Falanaras’s patrol passes through Tranquillien during a fighting withdrawal after destroying a necromantic focus elsewhere in the Ghostlands. The ruined town remains empty, hostile, and unheld: no banner, garrison, settlement, or lasting blood elf/Forsaken foothold is established.
properties.chapter16Continuity: The Silvermoon delegation sees Tranquillien from a ridge while the town is still ruined, hostile, and unheld. At Windrunner Spire, Sylvanas demands that blood elf and Forsaken forces clear and rebuild it as a joint base of operations. The provisional agreement preserves Quel’Thalas’s sovereignty and grants the Forsaken no separate territorial claim, while establishing paired blood elf–Forsaken command, agreed garrison limits, jointly counted stores, shared intelligence, and coordinated strikes toward Deatholme. The base is agreed in Chapter 16 but has not yet been built during the delegation’s journey.
properties.description: A ruined and hostile site in the Ghostlands on the contested road north of Deatholme. At the time of the Blood Knights’ first deployment, Tranquillien is not a blood elf outpost, garrison, settlement, or joint foothold; the Ghostlands remain wholly hostile, and the Chapter 12 battle occurs north of the runestone boundary inside southern Eversong.

A Horde-held settlement in Hillsbrad under constant pressure from Alliance forces based at Southshore. Its defense becomes the blood elves’ first military assignment after joining the Horde and brings Falanaras into direct conflict with Edric Hale.

The shattered world beyond the Dark Portal where Kael’thas’s summons draws Falanaras into alien alliances, the campaign against Tempest Keep, and M’uru’s capture. Silvermoon first regards Outland as a promised future, then severs that hope when Kael’thas turns toward demonic power.
The battlefield of the blood elves' first campaign as formal members of the Horde, where Falanaras faces Edric among the Alliance and glimpses Caelir from afar.
A dangerous mountainous region crossed by the blood elf retinue on its journey through Outland toward Netherstorm.

The naaru fortress in Netherstorm that Kael’thas’s forces assault in order to capture M’uru. Its inner shrine turns the campaign’s promised salvation into a morally troubling victory when M’uru receives the blood elf captors without meaningful resistance.

properties.bc_travel_note: Since The Burning Crusade, an Orb of Translocation connects the Undercity/Ruins of Lordaeron area to the Inner Sanctum of Sunfury Spire in Silvermoon City. The Undercity orb is in a newly opened city section west off the main part of the Ruins of Lordaeron; the city also has flight, zeppelin, and teleport connections.
properties.blood_elf_reaction_context: For living blood elves, Undercity plausibly reads as both a practical diplomatic center and an image of former horrors: a buried Lordaeron ruin inhabited by the dead, ruled by the former Ranger-General of Silvermoon, scented by corpse-stench and alchemy, and defended by powers the sin'dorei would once have found intolerable.
properties.chapter17Continuity: The Silvermoon delegation reaches the Ruins of Lordaeron by a controlled magisterial transit, then proceeds on foot through the shattered royal courtyard, the old throne room and Arthas’s remembered path, and iron elevators into Undercity. The Trade Quarter’s poisonous channels and multi-racial Horde traffic establish the living delegation’s discomfort. Sylvanas receives them in the Royal Quarter with Varimathras subordinate to her. The Horde admission council occurs below, while Falanaras’s controlled duel with Gorath takes place in the ruined courtyard above.
properties.description: The Forsaken capital beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron in Tirisfal Glades, built from old royal crypts, catacombs, tombs, dungeons, sewers, tunnels, caverns, and Scourge/Forsaken construction begun by Arthas and claimed by Sylvanas. It is a key site of blood elf diplomacy with Sylvanas and the wider Horde.
properties.layout: Roughly symmetrical quarters around a circular center: Trade Quarter at the bottom elevator exits, Magic Quarter northeast, Rogues' Quarter southeast, Apothecarium southwest, War Quarter northwest, Royal Quarter south from the Apothecarium entrance, Sewers west, and Canals between quarters. The city is reached through the ruined capital above and is more defensible than the city above it.
properties.notable_features: Royal Quarter with Sylvanas's throne; Apothecarium and Royal Apothecary Society; warlock/mage presence under Bethor Iceshard; Master Apothecary Faranell as a major apothecary figure; old Lordaeron throne room above with echoes of Arthas, Terenas, and Medivh; dead rose petals from Arthas's return; and the blood trail near the throne where Terenas's crown rolled.
properties.sensory_details: Sources describe Undercity as dark, cold, dreary, corpse-smelling, and almost unbearable for living Horde members because poisonous sludge, toxic fumes, and fetid odors permeate the city. Rivers or channels of poisonous sludge run through its avenues; spiders, oozes, and other subterranean creatures occupy distant passages. It is physically a refuge for the Forsaken and emotionally a place many living visitors experience as oppressive or wrong.

properties.description: The blood elf homeland, scarred by the Scourge invasion and struggling through reconstruction, hunger, and political isolation.
properties.directionalGeography: Canonical regional orientation is north-up. Quel’Danas lies north of Silvermoon; the Dead Scar runs north-south through Eversong Woods and the Ghostlands toward the Eastern Plaguelands.
properties.seasonalContinuity: Project adaptation: The Scourge attack disrupted the runestones that maintained Eversong Woods’ enchanted spring. Natural seasons briefly returned and the survivors endured winter until reconstruction restored enough of the runestone network to bring the spring enchantment back.

properties.chapter13Details: After months of regular traffic carrying military reports, supplies, couriers, and travelers between Silvermoon and Kael’thas’s Outland forces, the stabilized Dark Portal snaps shut without warning while travelers wait to cross. The near-side blood elf garrison remains intact, but the gateway becomes stone and darkness and all far-side contact ends. Silvermoon’s Azeroth-side relays continue to function; without Outland’s engines and power, Rommath judges a blind attempt to force the opening too dangerous.
properties.chapter14Details: After nearly eleven months closed, the Dark Portal is reopened when Doom Lord Kazzak drives an unidentified powerful artifact into the standing frame. Burning Legion forces cross from Outland before the field fully stabilizes, seize the lower stairs and approaches, and force the Azeroth-side blood elf garrison back to ridge fortifications. The gateway is active but hostile rather than restored as Silvermoon’s road. Concealed Farstriders can pass under extreme risk; they find altered or destroyed stabilizing engines, an abandoned Sunfury station, Legion-held ridges, and no blood elf formation controlling the Hellfire route.
properties.description: The threshold between Azeroth and Outland. In this story's continuity, Kael'thas's followers originally reached Outland by harder magical means after Dalaran; Illidan, blood elf magical expertise, and Outland engines later forced the Portal open from the far side, after which blood elves became the primary users and practical holders of the route while hostile or unfriendly Alliance/Horde/Kirin Tor observers largely avoided the crossing. After the later closure, Doom Lord Kazzak reopens it with an unknown powerful artifact for the Burning Legion, leaving the gateway demon-controlled until contested; Silvermoon can only scout and transit carefully by stealth magic at first.
The minor noble estate of Falanaras's family in Silvermoon, destroyed during the Scourge invasion. It is the site where he finds his father dead and loses his old life.
properties.invasionLocation: House Dawnspear stood in Silvermoon’s western quarter, which was destroyed and overrun during the Scourge assault. Falanaras leaves the viable eastern evacuation flow and crosses back into the lost western district to reach it.

properties.chapterDetails: Chapter 1 renders the Sunwell’s corruption during Arthas’s ritual as a bodily and spiritual violation felt across the surviving elves. Its later destruction after Kael’thas returns is established following the time skip in Chapter 2, where the resulting absence becomes the defining interior condition of the blood elves.
properties.description: The sacred font that once underlay all life in Quel'Thalas. Its destruction is not merely political or religious but bodily and civilizational: the removal of a constant ancient note beneath existence itself. The absence it leaves becomes the defining interior condition of the blood elves.

The emblem associated with Kael’thas and the blood elves’ hope of rising from destruction. When Silvermoon severs allegiance to the prince, removing his phoenix banners makes the political break visible and turns a symbol of promised renewal into a focus for grief and dissent.

Demonic magic adopted by the blood elves as a dangerous means of sustaining and rebuilding Quel’Thalas after the Sunwell’s destruction. Fel crystals and exposure mark sin’dorei bodies and public life, alarm outsiders, and provide effective power while carrying risks of corruption, dependency, and shame.

The arcane source that sustained Quel’Thalas and its people before Arthas corrupted and destroyed it. Its loss creates the blood elves’ magical hunger, spiritual rupture, and civilizational desperation, driving the survival practices and moral compromises at the center of the story.

properties.chapter12Proof: Inside southern Eversong, the first fourteen Blood Knights prove the order in field combat after an Amani-driven Scourge host breaches the runestone boundary. Each knight draws coerced Light through a personal connection to M’uru; those connections also replace mana crystals as routine relief from magical hunger. Strike, shield, and recovery files still use ordinary sin’dorei Mana Tapping tactically against hostile magic. They shatter undead bindings, hold an abomination, build a low, angled ward over a Forsaken withdrawal, reinforce it with additional force when death bolts threaten to break the span, and heal defenders quickly enough to contain the incursion. Liadrin teaches that more force is not failure: power must answer tactics, placement, command, and purpose. Appetite, panic, waste, cruelty, disobedience, and continuing after the objective ends are the dangers.
properties.description: The doctrine and practice by which each Blood Knight maintains an individual governed connection directly to the captive M'uru, wielding stolen Light without the devotional faith expected of traditional paladins. The connection can directly relieve magical hunger, so Blood Knights do not need mana crystals for routine relief, while every draw transmits an echo of M'uru's suffering. Blood Knights are trained to heal, protect, and strike with formidable force. Discipline means purposeful control—accurate placement, obedience to command and accepted terms, avoidance of waste and cruelty, and ending force when the objective no longer requires it—not habitual underdrawing or timidity. Their effective martial and medical use develops in parallel with Silvermoon’s unfinished effort to distribute M'uru’s relief safely to the whole population.

nodes.label: Stones of Light, Fire, and Spark

properties.description: Monolithic stones forming a magical network around Quel’Thalas. Historically they relayed the Sunwell’s power into Ban’dinoriel and helped maintain Eversong Woods’ perpetual spring.
properties.seasonalRestorationContinuity: Project adaptation: Arthas’s invasion damaged the runestone network and briefly allowed natural seasons, including winter, to return to Eversong Woods. During reconstruction, the blood elves restored enough of the network to renew the forest’s perpetual-spring enchantment.

properties.description: The sacred power once served through faith by priests such as Liadrin and wielded devotionally by paladins such as Edric. After M’uru’s capture, the Blood Knights force that power into martial service, making the Light both an effective means of protection and a constant reminder of sacred coercion.

properties.description: In this project, Wretched are blood or high elves whose magical dependency has tipped into compulsive overindulgence, social collapse, and loss of higher reasoning. They are mana-crazed, shunned, dangerous, and fixated on another feed; their horror lies in minds and identities collapsing around consumption. They are distinct from the nightborne Withered and are not framed as people suffering simple magical starvation. In the post-Sunwell era they seek relief by mana-tapping whatever sources are available.

properties.combatDoctrine: Mana tapping in battle is normal, necessary, and available to trained sin’dorei regardless of profession. Blood elves may tactically drain hostile spells, casters, enchantments, constructs, or other magical reservoirs to weaken an enemy and replenish themselves. The balancing act concerns how much they take and whether they stop; ordinary use is not treated as shameful or forbidden. Spellbreakers remain specialists in identifying, suppressing, redirecting, and stealing complex magic, but Mana Tap itself is a racial faculty rather than a spellbreaker-exclusive technique.
properties.description: In this project, Mana Tap is an innate blood elf faculty recovered, taught, and normalized across sin’dorei society after the Sunwell’s loss. By the present era, blood elves of every martial and magical discipline have learned to draw power from external magical sources and active enemy magic. Controlled use sustains ordinary function and gives blood elf forces an unparalleled baseline anti-magic danger regardless of formal training: in battle they routinely weaken spells, casters, enchantments, and magical creatures by taking measured power for themselves. Their discipline is not abstinence. The accepted line is between a purposeful draw and compulsive overindulgence—continuing beyond tactical or physical need, losing judgment, fixating on the source, or surrendering control can erode identity and lead toward Wretched degeneration.

properties.value: Blood elf life after the fall should constantly reflect magical hunger as physical withdrawal, spiritual loss, cultural trauma, and normalized mana-feeding rather than a single repeated conversation topic. Silvermoon is marked by visible fel crystals, enchanted rooms, mana sources treated like warmth or air, and the threat of Wretched degeneration. Characters may speak of “the hunger,” “the ache,” “the craving,” or “the emptiness,” but often communicate concern indirectly: offering a mana crystal, steering someone toward an active ward, noticing fixation on an artifact, or quietly registering exhaustion and tremors. Magisters rationalize dependence as physiology, rangers tend to distrust magical overreliance, Blood Knights redirect need into ritual and discipline, and commoners suffer most from uneven access to safe sources. Wretched outbreaks trouble places like Murder Row and areas outside the city’s order as mana-crazed collapse into compulsive feeding and social terror.

Among the Horde, the orcs are especially wary of blood elf fel use because of their own history of demonic corruption. They react strongly to sin'dorei green eyes, compare them to orcish green skin, and speak openly against allying with fel-tainted power again.

Outside observers generally find blood elf fel use and mana-feeding habits deeply unsettling, and this should recur whenever sin’dorei interact with outsiders. Returning high elves react with disgust and horror to fel crystals, mana-tapping, and the green tint in sin’dorei eyes, while the Forsaken are comparatively unfazed. Internally, blood elves rarely discuss their condition in blunt confessional terms; they mask it through euphemism, discipline, observation, and practical offers of relief. Close companions notice tremors, distraction, glassy focus on magical sources, irritability in magically dead places, or overcontrolled poise, while public culture treats visible loss of control as shameful.

When referring generally to hostile undead creatures or military groups, use ‘the undead,’ ‘the Scourge’ with plural agreement, or ‘Scourge forces.’ Do not use ‘the dead’ as a collective label for undead enemies. Specific creature terms such as ghoul, corpse, skeleton, deathguard, necromancer, or acolyte are appropriate when known. Ordinary uses of ‘dead’ remain valid for deceased individuals, dead vegetation or matter, the proper name Dead Scar, and adjectival descriptions of a specific body.

For this story’s adapted continuity, the Dark Portal remained closed after the old wars. Kael’thas, Lady Vashj, and their followers initially reached Outland after escaping Dalaran by harder, narrower magical means. Later, Illidan’s power, blood elf expertise, and Outland’s engines forced the Portal open from the far side and stabilized it for couriers, supplies, soldiers, and limited travelers. Kael’thas’s blood elves became the primary users and practical holders of the route; Alliance, Horde, Kirin Tor, Nethergarde, and other observers knew this but largely avoided the crossing while relations remained hostile or unfriendly. During a later closure lasting roughly a year, blood elf forces continued to hold and watch the Portal grounds until Doom Lord Kazzak used an artifact of unknown but tremendous power to reopen the gateway for the Burning Legion. The reopened Portal is initially demon-controlled rather than a safe Silvermoon road, though blood elf magisters can use careful stealth transit and magical scouting to assess Hellfire Peninsula and receive or verify a Scryer messenger from Shattrath.

Beginning with the first successful bindings in Chapter 11, every Blood Knight holds an individual governed bond directly to the captive M'uru. Liadrin is the first recipient, strongest early wielder, and leader of the order, but she is not a conduit through whom the other knights draw. A Blood Knight can use the personal connection to relieve magical hunger directly and therefore does not need mana crystals for routine relief, though ordinary Mana Tapping remains available for tactical use against hostile magic. Every draw of Light or hunger relief carries an echo of M'uru's pain. Blood Knights may use the full force required for victory, defense, healing, or mission success; discipline does not mean habitual underdrawing. Each knight is responsible for purposeful control: placing power accurately, obeying command and accepted terms, avoiding waste and cruelty, and ending force when the objective no longer requires it. This continuity supersedes earlier descriptions of Liadrin as the central living conduit and earlier framing that treated refusing available power as the primary mark of mastery.

Use the attached canonical regional map of Quel’Thalas as the directional reference, with north at the top. During the Scourge invasion, the undead advance from the south along the Dead Scar, pass through Silvermoon, and continue north toward Quel’Danas and the Sunwell. South is therefore the enemy approach and cannot serve as the general civilian escape route. Civilians and retreating defenders attempt to leave through side gates; the eastern side-gate route is the successful evacuation corridor. Silvermoon’s western approaches and western quarter are destroyed and overrun. House Dawnspear stands in that lost western quarter, so Falanaras must leave the eastern evacuation flow and cross west to reach it.

properties.value: Before Kael’thas renames the survivors sin’dorei after the Scourge invasion, Quel’Thalas’s high-elven civic, military, ranger, priestly, noble, and royal regalia should be described primarily in blue, silver, and white. The later cultural emphasis on red, crimson, and gold belongs to the blood-elf identity after the renaming and should not be back-projected onto pre-fall uniforms or banners. This constraint does not prohibit colors intrinsic to a subject or phenomenon, including red-gold hair, blood, fire, golden Holy Light, or red crystal architecture.

properties.description: The undead army that destroys Quel’Thalas, corrupts the Sunwell, and leaves the Dead Scar across the kingdom. Its surviving forces infest the Ghostlands and Deatholme, driving the battles that shape Falanaras’s early military life and the Blood Knights’ first deployment.

properties.chapter17Continuity: The Horde formally admits the blood elves of Quel’Thalas as sovereign members after political scrutiny and Falanaras’s controlled duel with Gorath. Admission requires blood elf troops to answer Horde calls, roads and intelligence to support common defense, leaders to participate in council, and sin’dorei forces to treat Darkspear, tauren, and Forsaken lives as equal obligations rather than expendable shields. Membership is legally established before broad trust or belonging.
properties.description: The coalition Silvermoon joins after severing allegiance to Kael’thas and finding no viable path back to the Alliance. Its leaders admit the blood elves under sharp reservations about fel corruption and M’uru, then test their commitment through the defense of Tarren Mill and the renewed war at the Dark Portal.

The sin’dorei survivors of Quel’Thalas, renamed blood elves in memory of their dead. Magical hunger, fel dependence, political isolation, and Kael’thas’s distant promises drive them toward M’uru’s captive Light, the Blood Knights, separation from their prince, and an uneasy place in the Horde.

properties.chapter13Details: Over several months, the Blood Knights become a seasoned field order through repeated boundary defense, dangerous Ghostlands missions, healing, forceful wards, and limited signal-based coordination with Forsaken scouts. Their first expansion beyond Silvermoon begins when Liadrin and Astalor connect Sanguinar and three Outland soldiers directly to M’uru. Sanguinar’s substantial tactical use of Light is legitimate; his corruption appears when he violates the spar’s target restriction, ignores yield, continues after Daric falls, and uses suffering as permission. The Portal closes after the Outland group returns, leaving those distant connections unmeasurable from Silvermoon.
properties.chapter17Details: The Blood Knights become a central subject of Silvermoon’s Horde admission. Liadrin admits before the council that their effective healing and force come through the suffering of a captive being of Light, while keeping M’uru’s identity secret. Falanaras represents the order in a controlled duel with Gorath Stonebinder and proves that one knight can withstand earth, wind, and lightning, answer with overwhelming red-gold force, and keep that power governed by tactical placement, command, and the duel’s accepted terms. He does not dismiss the Light until Gorath yields. The test demonstrates military power and martial discipline without resolving the moral objection to the order’s source.
properties.description: The blood elf martial order founded by Liadrin around individual governed bonds directly to the captive naaru M'uru. Liadrin is the first recipient and leader, not a conduit for the others. Its black-and-crimson knights combine healing and protection with aggressive military discipline, and their personal bonds provide direct relief from magical hunger without routine mana-crystal use. Every draw also carries M'uru's pain. Public-distribution research continues separately while the order proves vital to Quel'Thalas.

Sylvanas’s undead people and the blood elves’ first viable potential allies after Quel’Thalas’s estrangement from the Alliance. Forsaken scouts cooperate with sin’dorei forces against an Amani-driven Scourge incursion inside southern Eversong, establishing battlefield evidence of mutual usefulness while the Ghostlands and Tranquillien remain hostile and unheld. That precedent later supports Sylvanas’s sponsorship of Silvermoon before the Horde.

Quel’Thalas’s ranger corps under Halduron Brightwing. Farstriders defend the runestone boundary, pursue Amani raiders, and fight beside the Blood Knights and Forsaken when a driven Scourge host breaches into southern Eversong, while retaining practical distrust of magical overreliance.

properties.chapter14Details: The Scryers’ existence becomes known in Silvermoon when one of their messengers crosses Legion-held Hellfire with concealed Farstriders. Voren’thal’s letter explains that his followers abandoned Kael’thas’s intended attack on Shattrath after his vision and surrendered their weapons before A’dal. They offer testimony and documentary evidence about Kael’thas’s break with Illidan and demonic contacts, but Silvermoon initially treats them as protected, potentially treasonous witnesses whose claims require independent verification.
properties.description: The blood elves who defect from Kael’thas under Voren’thal after his vision of their people restored beneath a naaru’s Holy Light. Their warning from Shattrath reveals Kael’thas’s betrayal and offers Silvermoon evidence of a future beyond addiction and demonic dependence.

The forest-troll enemies of Quel’Thalas whose long war with the elves shapes Ghostlands security and Horde suspicion. During the first Blood Knight deployment, Amani raiders drive a Scourge host north along the Dead Scar and through the runestone boundary into southern Eversong. Their hostility remains distinct from the later Darkspear position represented by Vol’jin.

The elves who retain their older identity and Alliance ties after Quel’Thalas’s fall. Returning exiles led by figures such as Vereesa and Caelir confront Silvermoon’s sin’dorei with their fel dependence, altered loyalties, and the cultural gulf dividing survivors of the same catastrophe.

Kael’thas’s blood elf military forces in Outland. Their organized campaign against Tempest Keep enables M’uru’s capture, and their staging grounds host the first systematic test of the captive naaru’s power before it is carried to Silvermoon.

Silvermoon’s arcane elite, responsible for magical policy, fel-supported reconstruction, M’uru’s containment, and much of the kingdom’s coercive authority. Under Rommath and Astalor, magisters turn dangerous power into systems of survival while suppressing unrest when state necessity demands obedience.

A neutral, multi-racial order based at Light’s Hope Chapel and dedicated to containing and destroying the Scourge in the Plaguelands. Its wider ranks include living Alliance veterans and Forsaken members, and its field discipline requires members and attached delegates to set factional hostility aside while serving under Dawn command. In the Ghostlands, an all-paladin Argent patrol fights beside blood elves and Serenya Duskrunner’s independent Forsaken Dark Rangers. When Edric Hale’s alarm at fel-tainted sin’dorei and undead allies threatens a postbattle confrontation, the Argent commander establishes the Dawn’s institutional tolerance by stating that Forsaken serve elsewhere in the order and commands every side to stand down.
